function: p. 9-10: MIMO channel estimation with a learned score-network channel prior inside annealed second- and third-order Langevin posterior sampling (Nu=64 users, Nr=16 antennas, 60% pilots).
system: p. 9: Channel estimation: base station with Nr = 16 antennas, Nu = 64 single-antenna users, 3GPP CDL-C; band not stated; no RIS.
method: p. 6, 10: Annealed pre-conditioned underdamped and third-order Langevin posterior sampling; score network (architecture of [57]) trained by denoising score matching as in [16] (unsupervised generative prior).
data_channel: p. 9-10: Simulated 3GPP CDL-C channels (TR 38.901) for the channel prior, score network trained as in [16]; detection uses Kronecker-correlated Rayleigh fading.
test_conditions: p. 9-10: SNR sweep on CDL-C with Nr = 16, Nu = 64 and 0.6 pilots per user; no other channel, array or pilot setting tested.
baselines: p. 7, 9: Channel estimation: Lasso, fsAD (non-learned), L-DAMP (unrolled, learned), first-order annealed Langevin with learned score [16]. Detection: MMSE, V-BLAST, sphere decoding, ML, RE-MIMO, OAMPNet.
metrics: p. 7-11: NMSE for channel estimation; symbol error rate for detection; running time per symbol; PSNR, LPIPS and FID for imaging.
complexity: p. 8-10: Detection O(NuNr min{Nu,Nr} + LT(Nu^2 + K Nu)) and ms/symbol runtime; channel estimation cost depends on the network, with L=58 versus 2311 iterations.
q1_support: p. 9: "(CDL)-C model, which is adopted in 5G specifications [56]"; [56] is 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 14) and the score network is trained as in [16] (p. 10); the detection experiment uses Kronecker Rayleigh, not counted.
q2_support: p. 9: "We consider Nu = 64 and Nr = 16." Channel estimation is evaluated on one CDL-C configuration over an SNR sweep (Fig. 2, p. 10); the remark that the method handles a varying number of users without retraining (p. 9) concerns the non-learned detector and is not tested.
q3_support: Non-learned: p. 9: "Lasso [50]: This is a compressive-sensing-based approach" (also fsAD); learned: p. 9: "L-DAMP [53], [54]: This method is a data-driven algorithm" (also learned-score Langevin [16]); on NMSE, p. 10: "methods outperform the other baselines for SNRs greater than" 0 dB.
q4_support: p. 8: "Regarding the computational complexity, for MIMO detection we first compute" the SVD, with order given; p. 9: "Running time comparison." in ms/symbol; for the learned estimator p. 10: "The computational complexity depends on the neural network in this case" with L=58 versus 2311 iterations.
q5_support: p. 7: "Code to replicate the numerical experiments can be found at https://github." followed by com/nzilberstein/higher-order-langevin (footnote 2).
notes: Included via the channel-estimation experiment: the score network (denoising score matching, reused from [16]) is the learned component, so area 2. The MIMO detection experiment (area 1) uses a closed-form prior and no learning. The framework is mainly a sampler with theory, so the reviewer should confirm that a learned prior reused from [16] counts as a learned method. q4: order and runtime are for the detector; the learned estimator gets only iteration counts and a qualitative statement.
